name: Croissants
desc: Laminated butter croissants made over a day: dough, butter block, three folds, overnight rest, proof, bake.

source.title: Homemade Croissant Recipe
source.evidence: Same dough by weight (605 g flour, 66 g sugar, 12 g kosher salt, 7 g active dry yeast, 214 g water, 120 g milk, 57 g butter) and the same 24-hour schedule; Nick's uses a larger 340 g butter block and a book fold.

ingredients.raw: 4 2/3 cups (605 g) all-purpose or bread flour, plus more for dusting
1 tbsp plus 1/2 tsp (12 g) kosher salt
3/4 cup plus 2 tbsp (214 g) water, at room temperature
1/2 cup (120 g) whole milk, at room temperature

steps: Twenty-four hours before serving, make the dough: in a stand mixer with the dough hook, combine the flour, sugar, salt, and yeast. Make a well, pour in the water and milk, and mix on low until a tight dough forms around the hook, about 5 minutes. Cover with a damp towel and rest 10 minutes.

With the mixer on medium-low, add the softened butter a piece at a time and mix until the dough is smooth and elastic, 8 to 10 minutes. Shape into a flat rectangle, wrap, and refrigerate overnight, at least 8 hours.
Butter block: pound and roll the cold butter between two sheets of parchment into an even 8-inch square about 1/2 inch thick. Wrap and refrigerate.

On a lightly floured counter, roll the dough into a 16 x 8 inch rectangle. Set the butter square in the center, fold the dough ends over it to meet in the middle, and pinch every seam closed so no butter shows.
Roll the packet lengthwise into a rectangle about 24 inches long and 1/4 inch thick, keeping the edges straight. Fold it in thirds like a letter, wrap, and refrigerate 45 minutes.
Repeat the rolling, letter fold, and 45-minute chill twice more, for three folds total.
Roll the dough into a 16 x 14 inch rectangle about 1/4 inch thick. Cut it into four 4-inch-wide strips, then cut each strip corner to corner into 2 long triangles.
Roll each triangle from the wide base to the tip, tuck the tip underneath, curve the ends inward, and set on parchment-lined baking sheets with space between.
Cover loosely and proof at room temperature (70 to 75°F) until visibly puffy and jiggly, 2 to 3 hours.
Preheat the oven to 400°F. Brush the tops with egg wash, keeping it off the cut layers.
Bake until deep golden brown and hollow-sounding, 18 to 22 minutes. Cool on a rack at least 15 minutes.
tips: Proof below 75°F; a warmer spot melts the butter out of the layers and the croissants bake up dense.
If the butter starts to smear or the dough springs back while rolling, wrap it and freeze 15 to 20 minutes before continuing.
Nick's Kitchen uses a 340 g butter block and bakes at 350°F for 35 to 40 minutes; this version uses less butter and a hotter, shorter bake.
Salt is by weight: 12 g is about 1 tbsp plus 1/2 tsp of Diamond Crystal kosher salt. With Morton kosher, weigh it or use about 2 tsp.

references.title: Homemade Croissant Recipe
references.usedFor: 8 to 10 minute butter mix, 16 x 8 inch dough, sealing the packet, final 16 x 14 inch rectangle and triangle cut, 70 to 75°F proof, freezing when the butter softens, yield of 8
